sarah: FYI customer ACME reported embeddings suddenly switched models, downstream similarity index failing due to dimension mismatch. They say their integration has always sent the project key and expected 768-dim vectors, but responses are 1536-dim.

sarah: Customer repro (redacted key):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj_abc123" 
  -H "X-Org: org-acme" 
  -H "X-Project: acme-prod" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input": "hello world", "model": "embed-small-v1"}'
```

sarah: Response headers looked normal but payload shows model: "embed-large-v2" and length 1536. Customer says they never changed model. They hit post-deploy behavior after we rolled org-key fallback in routing last week.

raj: Can you paste the raw HTTP request/response bodies (headers + server routing trace) from the customer's capture? Need to verify whether the server accepted the project key or picked the org default.

sarah: Pasted the capture from their proxy (sanitized):
```
Request: Authorization: Bearer sk-proj_abc123
X-Org: org-acme
X-Project: acme-prod
Body: {"input":"hello world","model":"embed-small-v1"}

Response: 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"model":"embed-large-v2","embedding":[...1536 floats...]}
```

sarah: Also attaching our internal router trace (excerpt):
```
[2026-02-21T15:02:12Z] route-eval: received request, auth=org_key_present, project_header=acme-prod
[2026-02-21T15:02:12Z] policy: prefer_org_key=true
[2026-02-21T15:02:12Z] resolved_model=org-default/embed-large-v2
[2026-02-21T15:02:12Z] selected_backend=gpu-pool-7
```

raj: Thanks. That trace nails it — policy flip `prefer_org_key` caused the org default to override project-level model selection. We accidentally shipped the fallback as default behavior; intended flag was `prefer_org_key=false` unless customer opts in.

emily: Agree. Router code path `resolve_model_for_request` changed in commit 9f3b2c to treat any present org key as higher precedence. Quick diff:
```diff
- if project_header present: use project model
- else if org_key present: use org default
+ if org_key present: use org default
+ else if project_header present: use project model
```

emily: That reorder was a simple mistake during the fallback feature PR. It explains why customers who send both project keys and org headers now get the org default.

mike: Customer impact: ACME's semantic search index started returning garbage yesterday evening. They reported 2 downstream incidents and asked for rollback + credits. They are on a paid Dedicated plan.

raj: Actionable repro for us: use a valid project key and set X-Org header simultaneously. Repro steps: 1) curl with project key + X-Org, 2) request model embed-small-v1, 3) observe returned model embed-large-v2 and embedding length 1536.

raj: Quick local test I ran against staging shows same behavior. Example:
```bash
export AUTH=Bearer sk-proj_test123
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: $AUTH" 
  -H "X-Org: org-test" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input":"test","model":"embed-small-v1"}' | jq .model
# returns "org-default/embed-large-v2"
```

emily: Hotfix options: 1) revert commit 9f3b2c in router (fast), 2) toggle feature flag to keep `prefer_org_key=false` (very fast), 3) patch logic to explicitly prefer `X-Project` if project key present (correct fix). Recommend toggle flag + patch.

mike: Customer-facing plan: apologize, explain we found routing bug, immediate mitigation is to avoid sending X-Org header (if feasible) or send only project key with header `X-Override-Model: embed-small-v1` (we can support a temporary bypass). Also offer 2 weeks of credits and a postmortem. 

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1873 (severity: high) — assigned to @emily, @raj.

raj: I'll prepare a patch to enforce project key precedence and add unit tests. ETA 2 hours for feature-flagged rollback, 6 hours for full patch + deploy.

emily: I'll flip the feature flag in staging now and run smoke tests across Dedicated and Hosted. If green, we'll flip prod flag and monitor 15m.

sarah: Customer update drafted: short apology + status + mitigation steps + ETA. I'll send once we have flag flip result.

mike: Also note billing: embeddings unit counts are unchanged, but the customer used larger model so their bill spiked; finance asked for estimated overcharge so we can credit.

raj: Postmortem items: - revert or patch router precedence - add integration tests for header combinations (project key + X-Org + model param) - telemetry to emit resolved_model in access logs - docs update on header precedence

emily: I'll own deploy and telemetry. raj you own code patch. sarah you manage customer comms and credits. mike coordinate SLA credit approval.

sarah: I'll send interim message to ACME now: short note that we found issue, rolled a mitigation, ETA for full fix 6h, will follow up with credits and postmortem.

mike: Thanks team. Keep this thread updated with timestamps of flag flips and deploys.

ops-bot: flag toggled: prefer_org_key -> false (staging) at 2026-02-21T16:12:05Z

emily: staging smoke done, flipping prod now.

emily: flag toggled: prefer_org_key -> false (prod) at 2026-02-21T16:44:22Z

raj: Verified prod behavior after flag flip: project-specified model honored, embed dims back to 768 for ACME sample.

sarah: Sent customer update + credit promise. They acknowledged and are running their pipeline. :relieved:

mike: Closing loop with finance — will draft credit entry.

sarah: Postmortem ticket created: PM-2026-1873. Will write up root cause (router precedence change), timeline, impact, and remediation.

emily: Follow-ups: add a small e2e test harness that iterates header permutations. Also add a dashboard card for sudden model selection changes per org.

raj: Thanks everyone — good catch.
